territories.name: Middle Helladic communities
territories.label: Middle Helladic
territories.evidenceNote: Archaeological period zone, not a unified people or political border.

territories.name: Middle Cycladic communities
territories.label: Middle Cycladic
territories.evidenceNote: Generalised island culture-zone; chronology and material traditions varied between islands.

territories.name: Kushite-ruled Egypt (Twenty-fifth Dynasty)
territories.label: Kushite Egypt
territories.evidenceNote: Aggregate dynastic extent; Assyrian occupation is shown separately where the periods overlap.

territories.name: Saite Egypt (Twenty-sixth Dynasty)
territories.label: Saite Egypt
territories.evidenceNote: Dynastic Egypt centred at Sais; the map deliberately avoids a precise frontier in Nubia and the Levant.

territories.name: Independent Late Period Egypt
territories.label: Independent Egypt
territories.evidenceNote: Combined Twenty-eighth to Thirtieth Dynasties; internal political changes are not represented as fixed borders.

territories.name: Phoenician cities under Achaemenid rule
territories.label: Phoenician cities
territories.evidenceNote: Local Phoenician city identities continued within Achaemenid imperial rule; this is not a separate sovereign territory.

territories.name: Thracian regions
territories.label: Thracians
territories.evidenceNote: Broad cultural-geographic context only; Thrace contained multiple peoples and changing kingdoms, not a single continuous state.

territories.name: Illyrian regions
territories.label: Illyrians
territories.evidenceNote: Broad regional context for diverse communities and kingdoms; no single fixed Illyrian frontier is implied.

territories.name: Epirote communities and kingdom
territories.label: Epirus
territories.evidenceNote: Regional continuity is shown across major changes from independent communities to Molossian-led kingdom and federal organisation; no continuous single state is implied.
territories.sourceLabel: Politics, Territory and Identity in Ancient Epirus

territories.name: Etruscan city-states
territories.label: Etruscans
territories.evidenceNote: Cultural and city-state zone in west-central Italy; political control varied and contracted under Roman expansion.

territories.name: Carthaginian North African core
territories.label: Carthage
territories.evidenceNote: The core around Carthage is shown without converting its maritime alliances and trading network into a continuous territorial empire.

territories.name: Scythian regions north of the Black Sea
territories.label: Scythian regions
territories.evidenceNote: A mobile cultural region of diverse, mostly nomadic groups, not a single territorial state or fixed frontier.

territories.name: Kingdom of Cappadocia
territories.label: Cappadocia
territories.evidenceNote: Generalised dynastic core; alliances, overlordship and frontier control changed repeatedly.

territories.name: Kingdom of Bithynia
territories.label: Bithynia
territories.evidenceNote: Schematic kingdom zone; its frontiers with neighbouring Anatolian states changed across the Hellenistic period.
territories.sourceLabel: Met Pergamon and the Hellenistic Kingdoms

territories.name: Kingdom of Pontus
territories.label: Pontus
territories.evidenceNote: Retrospective conventional name for the Mithridatid kingdom; coastal, inland and dynastic reach changed substantially.

territories.name: Galatian polities
territories.label: Galatia
territories.evidenceNote: Central Anatolian zone associated with Galatian communities and rulers, not a stable uniform kingdom throughout the period.
territories.sourceLabel: Met Pergamon and the Hellenistic Kingdoms

territories.name: Armenian kingdoms
territories.label: Armenia
territories.evidenceNote: Broad Armenian political region; dynasties, client relationships and frontiers changed repeatedly between larger empires.

territories.name: Bosporan Kingdom
territories.label: Bosporan Kingdom
territories.evidenceNote: Small Greco-Scythian kingdom around the Cimmerian Bosporus; hinterland influence varied and is not shown as a precise border.

territories.name: Roman Hispania Citerior
territories.label: Hispania Citerior
territories.evidenceNote: Provincial command and expanding zones of control are simplified; unconquered northern regions are deliberately excluded.
territories.sourceLabel: National Atlas of Spain — Roman Hispania

territories.name: Roman Hispania Ulterior
territories.label: Hispania Ulterior
territories.evidenceNote: Generalised southern and western command zone; conquest and provincial control remained uneven during the Republic.
territories.sourceLabel: National Atlas of Spain — Roman Hispania

territories.name: Roman province of Africa
territories.label: Roman Africa
territories.evidenceNote: The initial province around former Carthaginian territory is shown schematically; later Numidian annexations are not back-projected to 146 BC.

territories.name: Roman Transalpine Gaul
territories.label: Roman Gaul
territories.evidenceNote: Mediterranean corridor later known as Gallia Narbonensis; exact organisation and inland reach changed over time.

territories.name: Caesar's conquests in Gaul
territories.label: Roman Gaul
territories.evidenceNote: Aggregate post-campaign control after 58–51 BC; resistance, client relationships and later provincial organisation are not shown as exact borders.

territories.name: Roman Cyrenaica
territories.label: Cyrenaica
territories.evidenceNote: Coastal Cyrenaican province shown schematically; desert and client-zone boundaries were not fixed modern frontiers.
territories.sourceLabel: Oxford map of Roman provinces in 44 BC

territories.name: Roman Crete
territories.label: Roman Crete
territories.evidenceNote: Crete was joined administratively with Cyrenaica; the island outline is shown as a simplified provincial zone.
territories.sourceLabel: Oxford map of Roman provinces in 44 BC

territories.name: Roman Cilicia
territories.label: Roman Cilicia
territories.evidenceNote: Pompeian-era provincial zone; the relationship between coastal districts, client rulers and inland regions remained changeable.
territories.sourceLabel: Oxford map of Roman provinces in 44 BC

territories.name: Roman Bithynia and Pontus
territories.label: Bithynia & Pontus
territories.evidenceNote: Pompeian settlement in northern Anatolia shown as a broad provincial zone; client arrangements and boundaries remained complex.

territories.name: Cypriot kingdoms under Saite Egyptian suzerainty
territories.label: Egyptian Cyprus

routes.evidenceNote: Generalised inland route through Arachosia and Drangiana to Carmania; it represents a detached force rather than Alexander's own Gedrosian march.
